solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In residence at college, I don't know what's needed to get through the gate

definitions.text: what's needed to get through the gate

parts.note: a student who lives in at a school or college is boarding there
in a quiz, saying 'pass' admits you don't know the answer

explanation.surface: A student living in at college, bewildered by what it takes to get past the gate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gate' looks like the college gate, but it is the departure gate at an airport.
explanation.definitionFit: At an airport you show this card at the departure gate before you may get on the plane.

clue.text: Wonderful location girlfriend finds nearly remote

parts.note: baby is an affectionate name for a girlfriend

indicators.note: nearly means the word for remote stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: remote means isolated or lone

explanation.surface: A girlfriend discovers a marvellous spot that is almost cut off from the world.
explanation.walkthrough: The city held the Hanging Gardens, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient city was home to one of the Seven Wonders, so it is literally a site of a wonder.

clue.text: It could be a dreadful recital

indicators.note: a dreadful performance is a mess, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Something that might turn out to be an awful performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the single letter 'a' in the clue, given by example: 'a' is the indefinite part of speech of that kind in grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the words 'a', 'an' and 'the' belong to this class of determiners.

clue.text: Target old man having consumption drowned by loud noise

indicators.note: having means the word for old man holds the rest within it

parts.note: old man is slang for father, dad

indicators.note: drowned by means the illness is swallowed up inside the noise

parts.note: a roar is a loud noise
TB, tuberculosis, was once called consumption

explanation.surface: An old man with tuberculosis is drowned out by a din.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub dartboard is the target the players throw their darts at.

clue.text: Rover with marbles intact, having lost shirt

indicators.note: having lost means one letter is dropped from the phrase for sane

parts.note: someone who still has their marbles is sane, not mad
a T is a shirt, as in T-shirt

explanation.surface: A wanderer who is still sane, though he has lost the shirt off his back.
explanation.definitionFit: A rover wanders from place to place with no fixed home, like a wandering herder.

clue.text: Silly commotion following pirate's first thrust

indicators.note: following means the commotion word comes after the rest
first means just the opening letter of pirate's is used

parts.note: a silly person is an ass
ado is fuss or commotion

explanation.surface: A foolish fuss that comes after a pirate's opening lunge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' is a noun here in sense, a fool; the fencing term is old-fashioned, met mostly in Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: In fencing this is a forward thrust made with one foot advanced, an old word for a lunge.

clue.text: Invoke response? We do turn litmus a shade of indigo

definitions.note: the definition is plural: these things speak, saying they do provoke a reaction

indicators.note: turn means the letters of litmus are changed round into another order
a shade of means only a hint of indigo, its first letter, is used

explanation.surface: Litmus paper changing colour to a hint of indigo, as in a chemistry lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' looks like litmus changing colour, but it signals rearranging LITMUS as STIMUL; add I from 'a shade of indigo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stimuli are things that provoke a reaction, so they can say of themselves that they invoke a response.

clue.text: Needled, I am king, on the face of it totally untidy

definitions.meaning: the tree speaks: a needle-bearing conifer, king among Christmas trees

definitions.text: on the face of it totally untidy
definitions.meaning: taken literally, the three words say 'in no way neat', so totally untidy

explanation.walkthrough: Split into three words, the answer reads 'nor way spruce': not in any way neat. The first half is the conifer speaking for itself; 'needled' means having needles.
explanation.definitionFit: This conifer with needles is the traditional Christmas tree, the one Norway sends to Trafalgar Square each year.

clue.text: To give an example, Telstar Records initially breaking in cursorily

indicators.note: breaking in means that letter forces its way inside the Latin word

parts.note: obiter, Latin 'by the way', means in passing, as in obiter dictum

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter of Records is used

explanation.surface: Telstar records cut in briefly, given as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: Telstar was an early communications satellite (also a 1962 hit record by the Tornados), so the surface's records mislead.
explanation.definitionFit: Telstar was a satellite circling the Earth, an example of a craft in orbit.

clue.text: Popular piece to confuse one that's nice!

parts.note: to mess something up is to confuse it
I is the Roman numeral for one
ah is an exclamation of pleasure

explanation.surface: A well-loved tune that muddles a listener into sighing with pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: Handel's oratorio is one of the most performed and best-loved choral works.

clue.text: Please, no way, woman on edge — why at auction?

indicators.note: on edge means the woman stands at both edges of the way, enclosing it

parts.note: hen is slang for a woman
Ave is the abbreviation for avenue, a way
what for? asks why, and a bid is an offer at auction

explanation.surface: A frantic plea: a woman on edge asks why anyone would bid at the sale.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an exclamation hoping something never happens, a fervent 'please don't'.

clue.text: Schoolboy howler?

parts.note: a howler is a schoolboy's blunder, but here it is a young animal that howls, which is also a junior Scout

explanation.walkthrough: 'howler' suggests a bad mistake in an exam, but read literally it is something that howls: a young wolf, and the name for the youngest Scouts.
explanation.definitionFit: A young wolf howls, and the junior branch of the Scouts takes its name from it.

clue.text: Batty night flight when this blood count's low?

definitions.text: Batty night flight when this blood count's low?

parts.words: Batty night flight when this blood count's low
parts.note: a vampire count takes bat form and flies at night to feed when short of blood

explanation.walkthrough: 'blood count' sounds like a medical test, but the Count is a nobleman who drinks blood and turns into a bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Bram Stoker's vampire Count turns into a bat and flies off at night to feed on blood.

clue.text: Writer's energy supporting central characters in Carry On Girls

indicators.note: supporting means the energy letter comes after, propping up the rest
central characters in means only the letters in the middle of the film title are kept, its outer runs discarded

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An author's energy backs the lead actors of a Carry On film.
explanation.walkthrough: Carry On Girls is a 1973 film in Britain's long-running Carry On comedy series.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte Mary Yonge was a prolific Victorian novelist, author of The Heir of Redclyffe.

clue.text: Sexy goddess emerging dazed from pit? Oh, dear!

indicators.note: dazed means confused, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A seductive goddess staggers out of a pit, muttering 'Oh dear!'
explanation.definitionFit: She is the Greek goddess of love and desire, the counterpart of Venus.

clue.text: The jollity, greeting an unlucky influence in the audience

indicators.note: in the audience means as heard by the listeners, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: hi is a greeting and a jinx is something that brings bad luck

explanation.surface: Merriment at a show, where a hello brings bad luck to the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means boisterous fun and frolics, a lively form of merriment.

clue.text: I may have at least two leads

definitions.text: I may have at least two leads

parts.words: I may have at least two leads
parts.note: the animal is walked on a lead and also follows leads, the clues in a case

explanation.walkthrough: 'leads' sounds like electric cables, but this animal is on a leash and also follows clues for the force.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog trained to help officers is kept on a lead and follows leads in an investigation.

clue.text: Like viral victim put on bottom bunk?

definitions.meaning: someone struck down by a virus is felled, confined by illness
literally placed at a low level, on the lower bed

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means struck down by illness, and literally describes being placed down low.

clue.text: Lovingly remark ruler's in preparation

parts.note: to coo is to murmur fondly
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A sweet remark that a monarch is getting ready.
explanation.definitionFit: Something being plotted or prepared is said to be on the go, as in 'what's cooking?'

clue.text: One getting paid out from demonstration

parts.note: a pro, a professional, is paid for their work
of can mean from, as in 'a man of Kent'

explanation.surface: Someone being paid off after a public protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demonstration' suggests a protest march, but it means showing something to be true.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence that establishes a fact demonstrates it, as in a mathematical demonstration.

clue.text: Composer's coup d'etat broadcast in one

indicators.note: broadcast means put out on air, so the word is heard rather than read, with the Italian spelling of its sound

parts.note: a putsch is a coup d'etat
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A composer is staging a coup that is being broadcast to all.
explanation.walkthrough: In Italian 'cc' before 'i' is said like 'ch', so PUCC sounds like the start of 'putsch'.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Puccini wrote the operas La Boheme, Tosca and Madama Butterfly.

clue.text: Extrovert prospect?

definitions.meaning: an extrovert looks outward, at the world rather than within
a prospect is a view or an expectation of the future

explanation.walkthrough: Split as 'out look', the answer describes the outward-facing nature of an extrovert.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a view ahead or the expected future, and literally an outward gaze.

clue.text: A fabulous creature, it has a rounded body, a narrowed mouth and a foot … Ulster firm invested

indicators.note: invested means placed within, like money put into the vessel

parts.words: it has a rounded body, a narrowed mouth and a foot
parts.note: this describes a vase-like vessel such as a funeral urn
NI is Northern Ireland, often called Ulster
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A description of a mythical beast, followed by a company putting money in.
explanation.walkthrough: The long middle stretch is a dictionary-style description of an urn.
explanation.definitionFit: This horse with one horn is a creature of fable and legend.

clue.text: Heart in one piece, but head lost — it's all relative

indicators.note: heart in means the middle letter of the word one is taken
head lost means the first letter of piece is dropped

explanation.surface: Despite a beheading, someone stays in one piece, since everything is relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family member, a relative.

clue.text: Being supposedly jolly, I hastily mend grate for Dr Spooner

indicators.note: Dr Spooner swapped the first sounds of words, so the two words swap their opening letters

parts.note: to tack is to sew roughly with long quick stitches
to jar is to grate on the nerves

explanation.surface: A fussy instruction to patch up a fireplace grate quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor is traditionally called a 'jolly Jack', so a cheerful seaman is this.

clue.text: Difficult to catch oriental assassin who's lost tail — and he's back on the turn

indicators.note: on the turn means the whole string is written backwards

parts.note: E is short for eastern, oriental

indicators.note: who's lost tail means the last letter of the assassin word is dropped

parts.note: an assassin is a killer

indicators.note: back means the end letter of the word he is taken

explanation.surface: An Eastern assassin, short a tail, has slipped away and is now coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the turn' reverses E + KILLE + E, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An eel is famously slippery, so something like one is hard to grasp.

clue.text: Capital bird touring capital city

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the last letter travels round to the front

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, capital, written here as AI
a robin is a bird

explanation.surface: An excellent bird flying round a capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like the definition but means A1, excellent; the definition is 'capital city'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the capital and largest city of Kenya.

clue.text: Cane used by military joker on force once in hospital rounds

indicators.note: rounds means encircles, so the word for ill goes around the rest

parts.note: someone in hospital is sick
a wag is a joker
g is the symbol for gravitational force
erst is an old word for formerly, once

explanation.surface: An army stick wielded by a comedian, from a hospital ward round.
explanation.definitionFit: Officers carried this short cane as a mark of rank and swagger.
